name: Paginated reports, mobile layouts, accessibility and personalization

why.matters: A report that can't be read on a phone, by a screen-reader user, or printed as a 40-page invoice list fails part of its audience, often the part that matters most.
why.failure: The regional sales report is used on phones in the field, but its mobile layout was never built; managers pinch and zoom, then ask for a PDF every Monday.
why.use: Paginated reports for pixel-perfect, printable, many-page output; mobile layouts for field users; accessibility settings (alt text, tab order, contrast, titles) for everyone; personalization so users adjust visuals without copies.
why.avoid: Colour as the only signal, interactive reports pretending to be printouts, and paginated reports for exploration.

verified.context: Paginated reports, mobile layout, accessibility and personalization docs (Microsoft Learn, Sept 2026)
verified.cert: PL-300 (2026-04-20): paginated reports, mobile, personalization, accessibility

asg.brief: Run the Beginner executive page through an accessibility review and fix what you find.
req: Alt text on every visual (what it shows, not "bar chart").
Tab order and titles; no information conveyed by colour alone; contrast checked.
Test with keyboard only and with a screen reader (Narrator or NVDA).
asg.exp: Every visual has meaningful alt text (ideally dynamic, from a measure), tab order follows the reading order, status uses icons or text as well as colour, and the page can be used with the keyboard alone.

asg.t: A mobile layout for field managers
asg.brief: Regional managers check sales on their phones between store visits. Build the mobile layout for the page they use.
req: Only the visuals that answer their question, in priority order.
Test in the Power BI mobile app or the phone emulator.
asg.exp: A portrait mobile layout with three to five visuals (headline numbers first), slicers at the top, no horizontal scrolling, tested in the mobile app.

asg.brief: Decide the right report type for four requests and justify each.
req: Monthly customer statements, one PDF per customer.
An exploratory dashboard of sales by region.
A 40-page price list printed for stores.
Commission statements emailed to each rep on the 1st (Sprint D05).
asg.exp: Paginated: statements, the price list and commission statements (fixed layout, many pages, per-recipient output, subscriptions). Interactive Power BI report: the exploratory dashboard.

int.q: When do you choose a paginated report?
int.a: When the output must be printed or exported with a fixed layout, spans many pages, lists detail rows (invoices, statements), or is generated per recipient. Interactive reports are for exploration and summaries.

int.q: What makes a Power BI report accessible?
int.a: Alt text on visuals, a logical tab order, titles and labels, sufficient contrast, not relying on colour alone, readable font sizes, and testing with keyboard navigation and a screen reader.
A setting that lets viewers change a visual's type, fields or aggregation for themselves and save it as a personal bookmark, without editing the report or making a copy.

int.q: Why build a mobile layout instead of relying on the phone showing the desktop page?
int.a: The desktop page shrinks to unreadable size. A mobile layout reorders and sizes visuals for portrait use, so the most important numbers appear first and controls are usable by touch.

ass.q: Statements must be emailed as one PDF per customer each month. Best fit:
o: Paginated report with a data-driven subscription or parameters

ass.q: A KPI turns red when below target, with no other cue. Accessibility problem?
o: Yes: colour alone conveys the status
ass.why: Add an icon, label or text so colour-blind and screen-reader users get the information.

ass.q: Enable personalization on one report page and test it as a viewer.
ass.hint: Report settings → Personalize visuals; viewers see the personalize icon on each visual.
